Estimate the slope of the nowcasted curve

Source: R/slope.estimate.quant.R
slope.estimate.quant.Rd

Fits a linear model to each trajectory returned by nowcasting_inla() or nowcasting_mgcv() (with trajectories = TRUE) within a given window. Requires the 'lme4' package. The default is 3 weeks. If 'end.week' is missing uses the maximum date in 'trajectories'.

Usage

slope.estimate.quant(end.week, trajectories, window = 3)

Arguments

end.week

(in weeks) The end of the week wanted to the slope estimate. Default: max. date in 'trajectories'.

trajectories

Data.frame with the predicted or nowcasted estimate

window

(in weeks) Window of how much time will be used to calculate the slope estimate. The default is 3 weeks.

Value

A trend category based on the distribution of the slopes of the trajectories: 1 increasing (5% quantile > 0), 0.5 probably increasing (25% quantile >= 0), 0 stable or uncertain, -0.5 probably decreasing (75% quantile <= 0) and -1 decreasing (95% quantile < 0).

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Loading Belo Horizonte SARI dataset
  data(sragBH)
  now <- nowcasting_mgcv(dataset = sragBH,
                         date_onset = DT_SIN_PRI,
                         date_report = DT_DIGITA,
                         trajectories = TRUE)
  slope.estimate.quant(trajectories = now$trajectories)
}
#> Warning: Using default, trimming out 0 days of data
#> Joining with `by = join_by(date_onset)`
#> Joining with `by = join_by(date_onset, delay, Time)`
#> Warning: Using max. date in 'trajectories' as 'end.week'
